Qinal's Anti-Piracy Summit: United Efforts to Combat Rising Piracy and Maritime Security Concerns

MOUSTAPAL - Prime Minister Reza Ngoda of Qinal hosted a crucial anti-piracy summit, bringing together leaders and representatives from the Xinan Economic Cooperation (XEC) and other Xinan nations, such as Xelina, Narashima, and Fenncao. The conference aimed to address the alarming rise in piracy incidents in the region and focus on developing a united and coordinated response to protect maritime interests and combat piracy funded by certain ATO nations and private military companies.

"Piracy poses a severe threat to our economies, maritime trade, and regional stability. It is essential for us to join forces and tackle this menace head-on, working together for the safety and well-being of our citizens," Ngoda stated.

The summit led to the signing of the "Moustapal Declaration," which included the establishment of joint naval patrols, enhanced intelligence sharing, and capacity-building initiatives for the nations involved. Additionally, representatives stressed the need to address the root causes of piracy, such as poverty, unemployment, and weak governance in some of the affected nations, as well as concerns over piracy being funded by certain ATO countries and PMCs.
